title: Articles: a, an and the
titleVi: Mạo từ a, an và the
summary: Khi nào dùng a/an, khi nào dùng the, và vì sao tiếng Việt khiến ta bỏ sót mạo từ.
whyItMatters: Tiếng Việt không có mạo từ, nên đây là lỗi khó sửa nhất và cũng dễ thấy nhất: *I am student*, *I like the dogs*. Giám khảo gặp lỗi mạo từ ở gần như mọi câu của thí sinh Việt Nam, và nó kéo điểm Grammatical Accuracy xuống đều đặn dù các cấu trúc khác đã tốt.

sections.heading: a/an: one of many
body: Use **a/an** with a **singular countable noun** when you mean "one of a group, not a specific one": *I saw a dog in the garden* (some dog, not a particular one).
This is why jobs and descriptions need an article: *She is a teacher*, *He is an engineer*, *Vietnam is a member of ASEAN.* The noun is countable and singular, so it cannot stand alone.
Choose **a** or **an** by **sound**, not spelling: *a university* (y-sound), *an hour* (silent h), *a European country*, *an MBA*, *a one-way street*.

rows: Take it twice a day. / 60 km an hour.
There is a problem with the data.

sections.heading: the: you know which one
body: Use **the** when the listener can identify the noun. That happens in four common ways: it was mentioned before, it is unique, it is defined by a phrase, or it is obvious from the situation.

*I bought a laptop. The laptop crashed.* (second mention) *The sun rose at six.* (unique) *The book on the table is mine.* (defined by *on the table*) *Could you close the door?* (only one door in the room).
**the** works with singular, plural and uncountable nouns: *the student, the students, the information.* This is the key difference from *a/an*, which only ever works with singular countable nouns.

rows: She adopted a cat. The cat is enormous.
The moon was bright last night.
The results of the survey were surprising.
It was the worst year on record.

sections.heading: a/an and the in the same paragraph
body: Academic and narrative writing alternate between the two constantly. The first mention introduces with *a/an*; every later mention uses *the*. Breaking this chain makes your writing sound like a list of unrelated facts.
Read the sequence: *A recent study examined a group of 200 students. The students were asked to keep a diary. The study found that...* Each *the* points back to something already established.

If you introduce a plural or uncountable noun, there is no *a/an* stage. *Researchers collected data from three schools. The data showed...* — the first mention has no article, the second takes *the*.

examples.right: The government introduced a new tax. The tax was unpopular.
examples.wrong: The government introduced new tax. Tax was unpopular.
examples.note: *tax* is countable here, so the first mention needs *a*.

examples.right: We interviewed a farmer and a shop owner. The farmer had lived there for 40 years.
examples.note: Second mention of one specific member.

examples.right: She wrote an essay on migration. The essay won a prize.
examples.wrong: She wrote essay on migration. Essay won prize.
examples.note: Singular countable nouns cannot stand alone.

sections.heading: Where Vietnamese speakers drop the article
body: Vietnamese marks definiteness with *một* (one) and with word order, not with a separate article. When you translate *Tôi là sinh viên*, nothing in the Vietnamese sentence corresponds to *a*, so the article disappears in English.

The fix is mechanical: before you finish a sentence, check every noun. If it is **singular and countable**, it needs **a/an**, **the**, **my/this/each**, or a number. A bare singular countable noun is almost always an error.
The reverse error also happens: learners add *the* to general plurals. *I like the dogs* means specific dogs you both know. For the species as a whole, English says *I like dogs.*

examples.right: My brother is a doctor at the city hospital.
examples.wrong: My brother is doctor at city hospital.

examples.right: Vietnam exports rice to the Philippines.
examples.wrong: The Vietnam exports rice to Philippines.
examples.note: Most country names take no article; *the Philippines* is a fixed exception.

sections.heading: Fixed expressions worth memorising
body: Some phrases are frozen and do not follow the logic above. Learn them whole rather than deriving them.

With *a/an*: *a few, a little, a lot of, as a result, in a hurry, have a look, make a decision, take a break, once a week.* With *the*: *in the morning, in the end, at the same time, on the whole, the other day, the more ... the more.*
With no article: *at home, at work, by car, on foot, in fact, for example, at night, go to bed.* These are the ones that most often get an unwanted *the*.

rows: go to bed / go to work
by bus / by train / on foot

commonMistakes.wrong: I am student at Hanoi University.
commonMistakes.right: I am a student at Hanoi University.
commonMistakes.why: Tiếng Việt *Tôi là sinh viên* không có mạo từ, nên người học bỏ luôn *a*. Danh từ đếm được số ít luôn cần mạo từ hoặc từ hạn định.

commonMistakes.wrong: I like the dogs because they are friendly.
commonMistakes.right: I like dogs because they are friendly.
commonMistakes.why: Nói về cả loài thì dùng danh từ số nhiều **không có mạo từ**. *The dogs* chỉ đúng khi nói về những con chó cụ thể mà người nghe đã biết.

commonMistakes.wrong: She is best student in my class.
commonMistakes.right: She is the best student in my class.
commonMistakes.why: So sánh nhất luôn đi với **the**: *the best, the most important, the first*. Đây là một trong số ít quy tắc không có ngoại lệ.

commonMistakes.wrong: He gave me an useful advice.
commonMistakes.right: He gave me a useful piece of advice.
commonMistakes.why: Hai lỗi: *advice* không đếm được nên không dùng *an*, và *useful* bắt đầu bằng phụ âm /j/ nên phải là **a**. Đếm được thì dùng *a piece of advice*.

commonMistakes.wrong: I have lived in the Vietnam for five years.
commonMistakes.right: I have lived in Vietnam for five years.
commonMistakes.why: Tên quốc gia thường **không có mạo từ**: *Vietnam, Japan, France*. Chỉ một số tên đặc biệt mới dùng *the*: *the Philippines, the Netherlands, the United States*.

ieltsTips: Trước khi nộp bài, quét lại mọi danh từ đếm được số ít — mỗi danh từ đó phải có `a/an`, `the`, `my`, `this` hoặc một số đứng trước.
Trong Task 1, dùng `the` cho số liệu đã xác định: `The figure for 2019 was 24%.` — không dùng *a figure* khi đã nói rõ năm.
Học cụm cố định theo khối: `as a result`, `in the long term`, `by bus`, `at night` — đừng suy luận từng từ.
Câu khái quát trong Task 2 thường **không có mạo từ**: `Unemployment remains a serious problem` — đừng viết *The unemployment*.

exercises.question: My father is ___ engineer at a factory in Bac Ninh.
exercises.explanation: *engineer* bắt đầu bằng nguyên âm /e/ nên dùng **an**.

exercises.question: I bought a phone last week, but ___ phone keeps freezing.
exercises.explanation: Lần nhắc thứ hai, người nghe đã biết chiếc điện thoại nào → **the**.

exercises.question: ___ unemployment in the north has fallen slightly.
exercises.explanation: *unemployment* là danh từ không đếm được, dùng khái quát nên **không có mạo từ**.

exercises.question: It took me ___ hour to finish the test.
exercises.explanation: *hour* có âm /aʊ/ bắt đầu bằng nguyên âm (h câm) nên dùng **an**.

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Children need the stability and the routine.
The children need the stability and routine.
A children need stability and a routine.
exercises.explanation: Hai danh từ không đếm được dùng khái quát → không mạo từ.

exercises.question: She wants to become ___ pilot after she graduates.
Could you pass me ___ salt, please?
exercises.hint: shared situation, unique on the table
exercises.explanation: Người nghe biết lọ muối nào → **the**.

exercises.question: He goes to work ___ bus every morning.
exercises.explanation: Cụm cố định **by bus** — không dùng mạo từ.

exercises.question: This is ___ most interesting book I have read this year.
He is ___ only person who knows the password.
exercises.explanation: *the only* là cụm cố định — *only* luôn đi với **the**.
